references.text: Just two verses later, Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper with the cup representing the new covenant in his blood ([ref:Luk 22:19-20|Luke 22:19-20]). The cup in verse 17 is likely the Passover meal cup that precedes the actual institution of the Lord's Supper.
Matthew's parallel account of the Lord's Supper, where Jesus takes the cup, gives thanks, and gives it to the disciples with words about covenant blood ([ref:Matt 26:27-29|Matthew 26:27-29]).
Mark's parallel account where Jesus takes the cup, gives thanks, gives it to the disciples, and they all drink from it ([ref:Mark 14:23-25|Mark 14:23-25]).
Paul's recounting of the institution of the Lord's Supper, where the cup is linked to the new covenant in Jesus' blood ([ref:1 Kor 11:25-26|1 Corinthians 11:25-26]).

The following verse where Jesus says he will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until God's kingdom comes ([ref:Luk 22:18|Luke 22:18]), giving an eschatological dimension to the cup in verse 17.
Paul refers to the cup of blessing that we bless as a sharing in the blood of Christ ([ref:1 Kor 10:16|1 Corinthians 10:16]). The term "cup" and thanksgiving link back to Jesus' action in Luke 22:17.

The original institution of the Passover meal in Egypt ([ref:2 Mos 12:1-14|Exodus 12:1-14]). Jesus celebrates the Passover with his disciples, and the cup in Luke 22:17 belongs to this traditional Jewish ritual.

"I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord" ([ref:Sal 116:13|Psalm 116:13]). This psalm was sung during the Passover meal, and the cup of salvation is linked to the thanksgiving of Passover, just as Jesus takes the cup and gives thanks in Luke 22:17.
